headline: Students requested $10,000 for the Sankofa Summit, and proposed charter amendments would exempt citizenship status information from public records.
summary: Four city groups presented their youth programs, and Councilor Sanchez-Parkinson said future talks will cover existing youth investments, shared goals, service gaps, and jobs and internships. Office updates covered the Language Access Policy and a winter clothing giveaway run with Street CATs, Fletcher Free Library, and AALV.

1. Call to Order 
a. Councilor Sanchez-Parkinson called the meeting to order at 5:35 pm. 
2. Approve Agenda & Minutes 
a. Councilor Carpenter moved to approve the agenda and meeting minutes. Councilor Sanchez-Parkinson 
seconded. The motion passed unanimously. 
3. Public Forum 
a. Keren Sita raised concerns regarding racial representation in crime reporting and policing practices and 
asked for continued attention to impacts on Black community members. 
b. Police Commissioner Romeo von Hermann introduced himself, expressed appreciation for the work of 
the REIB Committee, and stated his interest in learning from and supporting the committee’s efforts.  
c. Andre Clarke from Street CATs invited everyone to Contois for a community panel discussion on 
November 18th from 6:30-8:30 pm. The discussion was about homelessness, public safety, and 
substance use disorder. He shared information about the winter clothing and supply giveaway in 
partnership with the REIB, Fletcher Free Library, and AALV along with the donation drop-off locations 
(King Street Laundry, Fletcher Free Library, and AALV).
d. Students from Burlington High School, Grace Sunshine and Julie Dang, presented plans for the Sankofa 
Summit. They requested a $10,000 investment from the City to support programming, facilitators, 
materials, and accessibility. Refer to the video 
i. Councilor Grant expressed support and encouraged students to submit a written proposal for 
future funding discussions. Refer to the video. 
4. Office of REIB Updates 
a. Christian Berry updated the committee shared the City’s Language Access Policy continues to be 
implemented. “I Speak” posters were updated and will be redistributed throughout City facilities. More 
than 60 applications were received for the REIB Community & Belonging Program Manager role and an 
initial review process with interviews and screening will be completed. She shared the REIB is partnering 
with Street CATs, Fletcher Free Library, and AALV on the Winter Clothing giveaway and event materials 
were being translated for wider community outreach. She shared about the upcoming Soul Santa event. 
5. Non-Citizen Voter Protections Policy and Charter Amendments 
a. Councilor Allie Schachter provided an update on proposed charter amendments to protect citizenship 
status information associated with Burlington’s non-citizen voter program. Proposed amendments 
would exempt citizenship status and other identifying information from public disclosure through public 
records requests. Refer to the video. 
i. Councilor Grant noted support for the charter amendment while emphasizing ongoing concerns 
related to Fair and Impartial Policing policies and immigration-related community impacts. 
6. Supporting & Investing in Burlington’s Youth 
a. City Departments Burlington City Arts, Fletcher Free Library, Burlington Parks, Recreation, and 
Waterfront, and the REIB shared presentations about their youth programs. Refer to the video.  
7. Next Steps 
a. Councilor Sanchez-Parkinson discussed the importance of identifying opportunities for collaboration 
across youth-serving departments and organizations. 
i. She outlined future discussion will focus on: 
1. Existing investments in youth 
2. Shared goals and resources 
3. Service gaps and opportunities 
4. Employment and internship opportunities for youth 
8. Adjournment 
a. Councilor Sanchez-Parkinson adjourned the meeting at 7:35 pm.
